title: Patellofemoral Arthritis
note: Generated by tools/positions.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification, kind, signed_off_by and note fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. The detector over collects on purpose: mark anything that is teaching rather than clinical direction as NOT_CLINICAL rather than deleting it.

positions.as_written: Record the facet as well as the grade, because the distribution carries the mechanical message.
Read medial facet wear as a sign of overcorrection rather than as natural progression.
Expect symptoms in loaded flexion and relative comfort in full flexion, because of tendon load sharing.
Avoid inferring severity of symptoms from severity of wear.
The mechanical account of patellofemoral degeneration is more secure than the mechanical account of patellofemoral pain, and the two should not be run together.
Treat the link between predicted pressure and observed wear as a reasonable inference rather than a demonstrated sequence.
Expect offloading to help a mapped lesion more than an unmapped one, and counsel on that basis.

Weigh age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and the patient's own ideas, concerns and expectations, because an isolated pattern on imaging does not settle what operation suits the person.
